## 0 Overview

`Thesis_Replication` is the R folder behind the empirical chapters of
the bachelor thesis *Imperfect Credibility at the Effective Lower Bound:
A Behavioural Macroeconomic Analysis of Eurozone Inflation Expectations*
(University of St. Gallen, November 2026). Two scripts do the work.
`build_database.R` turns the raw downloads into a DuckDB database once.
`main.R` reads that database, classifies the forecasters of the ECB
Survey of Professional Forecasters (SPF), estimates the two behavioural
parameters of the expectations block and evaluates both models against
the SPF mean.

Research question of the thesis:

> To what extent does a time varying perceived inflation anchor improve
> the ability of the expectations block of a Behavioural New Keynesian
> model to explain euro area inflation expectations, particularly at
> the effective lower bound, and does any potential gain stem from the
> anchor itself or from agents switching between forecasting rules?

**Model A** is centred on the announced target of 2%. **Model B** is
centred on the perceived anchor built from the 5y5y inflation-linked
swap rate. **Model S**, centred on the mean SPF five-year-ahead
forecast, is the robustness check.

With its default parameters `main.R` reproduces Tables 4.2, 5.3 to 5.7,
6.1 to 6.4 and J.1 and Figures 4.1 to 4.3, 5.1 to 5.4, J.1 and J.2. Not
in the package are Table 4.3 and Figure 4.4 (capture ratios), Figures
J.3 and J.4 and the dashed Wald curves of Figure 5.2.

## 1 Getting started

### 1.1 Requirements

-   R 4.4 or 4.5 and RStudio
-   An internet connection for the first start, when `renv` installs
    the packages
-   No build tools. The packages come ready-built for Windows and macOS

### 1.2 Install

Extract the archive, open `Thesis_Replication.Rproj` in RStudio and run
this once in the console:

``` r
renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)
```

It installs the package versions of `renv.lock` into a project library
and takes about a minute. On a Mac, unzip to Documents rather than
Downloads.

### 1.3 First run

Open `main.R` and source it (the Source button, or Ctrl+Shift+S). The
default run takes about two and a half minutes. Tables appear in the
console, figures in the Plots pane. Nothing is written to disk.

### 1.4 Changing a parameter

Every parameter sits in Part I of `main.R` with its thesis value in a
comment. Change a value and source the script again. Every table and
figure follows. At the end the script lists the parameters that differ
from the thesis and checks Table 5.6 against the thesis values.

### 1.5 Rebuild the database (optional)

``` r
source("build_database.R")
```

The database ships ready, so this step is only needed if a raw file is
replaced. The script reads the raw files in `data/raw/`, saves every
cleaning step as its own table and prints the checks of the data
chapter. It takes under a minute.

## 2 How the folder is organised

| File | Purpose |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `main.R` | The analysis, one script read top to bottom |
| `build_database.R` | Builds `data/thesis.duckdb` from `data/raw/` |
| `data/raw/` | The raw downloads as obtained |
| `data/thesis.duckdb` | The database, 13 tables (Section 6) |
| `notebooks/user_guide.qmd` | This guide, rendered to `user_guide.html` |
| `renv.lock`, `renv/activate.R`, `.Rprofile` | The package versions |
| `README.md` | How to run it, in short |

`main.R` has ten parts. They are RStudio sections, so the document
outline (Ctrl+Shift+O) jumps between them.

| Part | What it does | Main objects |
|---------|---------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| Set up | Loads the packages | |
| I | Parameters | `anchor`, `score`, `delta`, the switches, `baseline`, `this_run` |
| II | Input checks | |
| III | Loads the data, builds the centres, calibrates the constants | `panel`, `rounds`, `premium`, `models` |
| IV | Model functions | the functions of Section 4 |
| V | Classification, Table 4.2 | `classified`, `shares` |
| VI | Estimation, Table 5.3 | `fit`, `results` |
| VII | Evaluation, Tables 5.4, 5.6 and 5.7 | |
| VIII | Side analyses, Tables 5.5 and 6.1 to 6.4, and Table J.1 | `real_time_biases` |
| IX | Comparison with the thesis | `changed`, `comparison` |
| X | Figures 4.1 to 4.3, 5.1 to 5.4, J.1 and J.2 | |

Every table and figure stays in the workspace as an object. Its name
starts with the thesis number and ends with a word for its content, for
example `table_5_6_gain` or `fig_5_2_profiles`.

`build_database.R` has eleven parts in the same style, one per source
and cleaning step.

## 3 Parameter reference (Part I of `main.R`)

Data inputs.

| Parameter | Thesis value | Meaning |
|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|
| `DB_FILE` | `"data/thesis.duckdb"` | The database |
| `TABLE_PANEL`, `TABLE_ROUNDS` | `"estimation_panel"`, `"rounds"` | The two tables the script reads |

Four switches change the specification.

| Parameter | Thesis value | Meaning |
|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|
| `anchor` | `"ILS"` | Centre of the second model. `"ILS"` gives Model B, `"LTSPF"` gives Model S |
| `score` | `"saturating"` | Performance score. `"saturating"` is Equation 5.2, `"msfe"` the squared error |
| `bias_statistic` | `"median"` | Statistic of the biases (Equation 5.5), `"median"` or `"mean"` |
| `bias_window` | `"complete"` | Rounds the biases are calibrated on. `"complete"` is the whole sample, `"pre ELB"` the rounds before `elb_from` |

Centres, sample and regimes.

| Parameter | Thesis value | Meaning |
|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|
| `target` | `2` | Announced target, in %. It also sets the level of Model B's centre |
| `first_round`, `last_round` | `"2004Q3"`, `"2026Q2"` | Estimation window, 88 rounds |
| `bench_from`, `bench_to` | `"2004Q3"`, `"2014Q2"` | Normalisation window of the perceived anchor (Equation 3.2) |
| `elb_from`, `elb_to` | `"2014Q3"`, `"2022Q2"` | ELB regime (Table 3.4) |
| `horizon` | `4` | Rounds between a forecast and its evaluation |

Calibrated constants. `NA` takes the value the thesis calibrates from
the data. A number overrides that one constant and leaves the others
unchanged, so the run shows its effect all else equal.

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|
| `delta` | `NA` (0.2824) | Half width of the targeter band (Equation 4.3) |
| `E_star` | `NA` (3.11) | Threshold between ordinary and extreme errors (Equation 5.7) |
| `tau` | `NA` (0.399) | Scale of the saturating score (Equation 5.6) |
| `w` | `NA` (0.101) | Weight of the squared error (Equation 5.6) |
| `bias_up`, `bias_down` | `NA` per model | Hawk and dove bias. `NA` calibrates it (Equation 5.5), a number fixes it |
| `U_0` | `0` | Performance of every heuristic before the first evaluation |

Optimiser and side analyses.

| Parameter | Thesis value | Meaning |
|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|
| `quick_mode` | `FALSE` | `FALSE` uses 300 starting values, `TRUE` 30. The package ships with `TRUE`, which gives the same estimates |
| `gamma_start_range`, `rho_start_range` | `c(0.01, 100)`, `c(0, 0.98)` | Ranges of the starting values |
| `run_feasibility` | `TRUE` | Table 5.5 |
| `run_anchors` | `TRUE` | Table 6.1 |
| `run_delta` | `TRUE` | Table 6.2 |
| `run_score` | `TRUE` | Table 6.3 |
| `run_biases` | `TRUE` | Table 6.4, the real-time rows of Table J.1 and Figures J.1 and J.2 |

## 4 Function reference (Part IV of `main.R`)

Three arguments recur. `model` is a model letter, `"A"`, `"B"` or
`"S"`. `data` is the list returned by `prepare()`. `score_set` holds
the settings of the score, made by `score_settings()`. Examples follow
in Section 5.

### 4.1 Classification and data of a model

#### \[1\] **`classify(forecast, centre, delta)`**

-   Assign each forecast to a type around its centre (Equation 4.1).

**Arguments**

-   `forecast`, `centre : numeric` vectors of the same length.
-   `delta : numeric`, half width of the targeter band.

**Returns**

-   A character vector with `"hawk"`, `"targeter"` or `"dove"`.

#### \[2\] **`classify_panel(model, delta)`**

-   Classify the whole panel around the centre of one model. The only
    place where forecasts are classified.

**Returns**

-   The panel with the columns `model`, `regime`, `centre` and `type`.

#### \[3\] **`prepare(model, delta, b_up, b_down, statistic, window, same_rounds)`**

-   Classify the forecasts around a centre, calibrate the two biases
    (Equation 5.5, done by `calibrate_biases()`) and collect the data
    of the scored rounds.

**Arguments**

-   `model`, `delta` as above.
-   `b_up`, `b_down : numeric or NA`, default the biases of Part I. `NA`
    calibrates the bias.
-   `statistic`, `window : character`, default the two bias switches of
    Part I. `window = "real time"` gives real-time biases (Table 6.4).
-   `same_rounds : logical`. `TRUE` scores constant biases on the
    rounds that real-time biases can use.

**Returns**

-   A list with the counts per round, the centres, realised inflation,
    the SPF mean and the two biases.

#### \[4\] **`score_settings(tau, w, msfe = FALSE)`**

-   Bundle the settings of the performance score.

**Returns**

-   `list(tau, w, msfe)`. With `msfe = TRUE` the score is the squared
    error.

### 4.2 The expectations block

#### \[5\] **`probabilities(gamma, rho, data, score_set)`**

-   The shares of the hawk, targeter and dove heuristic in every scored
    round (Equations 5.1 to 5.4).

The errors $e$ of the three heuristics against realised inflation are
scored by

$$
\psi(e) = \frac{e^2}{e^2 + \tau^2} + w\,e^2,
$$

accumulated into the performance
$U_t = \rho\,U_{t-1} - (1 - \rho)\,\psi(e_t)$ and turned into shares by
the multinomial logit.

**Arguments**

-   `gamma`, `rho : numeric`, intensity of choice and memory.

**Returns**

-   A matrix, one row per scored round, three columns that sum to one.

#### \[6\] **`minus_loglik(par, data, score_set)`**

-   Minus the multinomial log-likelihood (Equation 5.8), the objective
    of the optimiser.

**Arguments**

-   `par : numeric(2)`, `c(gamma, rho)`.

**Returns**

-   One number, 1e12 outside $\gamma$ in \[0, 1000\] and $\rho$ in \[0,
    0.999).

### 4.3 Estimation

#### \[7\] **`starting_values(n_gamma, n_rho)`**

-   The starting grid, log-spaced $\gamma$ times evenly spaced $\rho$.

**Returns**

-   A data frame with the columns `gamma` and `rho`.

#### \[8\] **`estimate(data, score_set, starts)`**

-   Nelder-Mead from every starting value, each search restarted once.

**Returns**

-   A list with `gamma`, `rho`, `loglik` and `searches`, the end point
    of every search.

#### \[9\] **`dispersion(data, prob)`**

-   The dispersion factor $\hat\varphi$ (Equation 5.10).

**Returns**

-   One number, 15.35 for Model A and 15.36 for Model B.

#### \[10\] **`standard_errors(gamma, rho, data, score_set, phi)`**

-   Standard errors from the Hessian, multiplied by $\hat\varphi$
    (Equations 5.11 and 5.12).

**Returns**

-   `list(se, correlation)`. Both are `NA` with a warning when the
    estimate lies at a bound or the Hessian cannot be inverted.

#### \[11\] **`fit_model(model, score_set, starts, delta_used = delta, statistic, window, same_rounds)`**

-   One complete fit of a model. Calls the functions above and forms
    the aggregate expectation (Equation 5.13) and its error against the
    SPF mean (Equation 5.14). `statistic`, `window` and `same_rounds`
    choose the biases as in `prepare()`.

**Returns**

-   A list with everything from `prepare()` and `estimate()`, plus
    `prob`, `phi`, `se`, `correlation` and `results`, a table with one
    row per scored round. The fits of the run live in `fit$A` and
    `fit$B` (or `fit$S`).

### 4.4 Evaluation helpers

#### \[12\] **`rmsfe(error)`, `mafe(error)`, `msfe(error)`**

-   Root mean squared, mean absolute and mean squared forecast error
    (Equation 5.14).

#### \[13\] **`with_full_sample(rows)`**

-   Repeat every row under the regime `"Full sample"`, so that a
    `group_by(regime)` also gives the full-sample line.

#### \[14\] **`summarise_fit(model_fit, variation)`**

-   One row in the layout of the Chapter 6 tables.

#### \[15\] **`both_models(variation, score_set, delta_used = delta)`**

-   Fit Model A and the second model under one setting from 30 starting
    values and return their two rows.

#### \[16\] **`show_variations(rows)`**

-   Print such rows in the thesis layout, each loss as "A / B".
    `layout_variations()` returns the same table without printing it.

Small helpers format numbers (`three()`, `two()`, `pct()`, `signed()`,
`wald()`),
check the parameters (`is_number()`, `is_number_or_na()`, `is_round()`),
date the regimes (`regime_of()`), pick one element from both fits
(`from_fits()`) and name a fit in a warning (`fit_label()`).

## 5 Outputs and examples

The chunk below runs `main.R` with its defaults. Each output is then
shown as the script produces it, followed by a variant that calls the
functions of Section 4 directly.

```{r}
#| label: run-main
#| results: hide
#| fig-keep: none
source("main.R")
```

### 5.1 The sample and the constants

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sample
#| tbl-cap: "Rounds by regime and the mean of the two centres."
knitr::kable(
  rounds |>
    group_by(regime) |>
    summarise(rounds = n(), first = min(round), last = max(round),
              `mean centre A` = mean(centre_A), `mean centre B` = mean(centre_B)) |>
    arrange(first),
  digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: premium
cat("Premium of the swap rate:", round(premium, 4), "\n")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-constants
#| tbl-cap: "The constants in use and the values implied by the data (4'001 forecast errors)."
knitr::kable(data.frame(used      = c(delta, E_star, tau, w),
                        from_data = from_data[c("delta", "E_star", "tau", "w")],
                        row.names = c("delta", "E_star", "tau", "w")), digits = 5)
```

### Output 1: Classification, Table 4.2

`classified` holds every forecast with its type, `shares` the three
shares per round and model.

**Default call:**

```{r}
#| label: tbl-4-2
#| tbl-cap: "Table 4.2: mean targeter share by regime, in %."
knitr::kable(table_4_2_shares, digits = 2)
```

**Variant** (a band twice as wide):

```{r}
#| label: ex-prepare-wide
wide <- prepare("A", delta = 2 * delta)
colSums(wide$counts)                      # hawks, targeters, doves over the 84 scored rounds
c(hawk_bias = wide$b_up, dove_bias = wide$b_down)
```

### Output 2: Estimates, Table 5.3

`fit$A` and `fit$B` are the two fits of the run.

**Default call:**

```{r}
#| label: tbl-5-3
#| tbl-cap: "Table 5.3: overdispersion, standard errors and confidence intervals."
knitr::kable(table_5_3_estimates)
```

**Variant** (Model B under the -MSFE score, 30 starting values):

```{r}
#| label: ex-fit-msfe
fit_B_msfe <- fit_model("B", score_settings(tau, w, msfe = TRUE), starting_values(6, 5))
knitr::kable(summarise_fit(fit_B_msfe, "-MSFE"), digits = c(NA, NA, rep(3, 9), 0))
```

### Output 3: Evaluation, Tables 5.4, 5.6 and 5.7

`results` holds one row per scored round and model. Table 5.6 splits
the fit into the centre alone and what switching adds. Table 5.7 starts
both models from the announced target alone and adds the location gain.

**Default call:**

```{r}
#| label: tbl-5-4
#| tbl-cap: "Table 5.4: model expectations against the mean SPF forecast, by regime."
knitr::kable(table_5_4_errors, digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-5-6
#| tbl-cap: "Table 5.6: RMSFE of the centre alone and of the complete model, in pp, and the switching gain."
knitr::kable(table_5_6_gain, digits = c(NA, NA, 3, 3, 3, 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-5-7
#| tbl-cap: "Table 5.7: RMSFE of the target alone, of the centre alone and of the complete model, in pp, with the location gain, the switching gain and the total gain."
knitr::kable(table_5_7_location, digits = c(NA, NA, rep(3, 6), 0))
```

**Variant** (the shares for a chosen pair, $\gamma$ = 1 and $\rho$ =
0.9, in Model A):

```{r}
#| label: ex-probabilities
shares_chosen <- probabilities(gamma = 1, rho = 0.9, fit$A, base_score)
knitr::kable(data.frame(round = fit$A$round, round(shares_chosen, 3))[1:5, ])
```

## 6 Database catalogue

`data/thesis.duckdb` holds thirteen tables. The raw tables keep the
downloads unchanged and every later table is one cleaning step.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-catalogue
#| tbl-cap: "The tables of the database with their number of rows."
con    <- dbConnect(duckdb(shared_home = FALSE), dbdir = DB_FILE, read_only = TRUE)
tables <- dbReadTable(con, "table_descriptions")
tables$rows <- sapply(tables$table, function(t) dbGetQuery(con, paste("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM", t))$n)
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
knitr::kable(tables)
```

The two tables `main.R` reads:

| Table | Column | Meaning |
|---------------|---------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `rounds` | `round`, `survey_date`, `target_date` | Survey round, its survey month and the month its forecast refers to |
| | `n_forecasts`, `spf_mean`, `spf_sd` | Point forecasts of the round, their mean and standard deviation |
| | `ils` | 5y5y inflation-linked swap rate of the survey month |
| | `hicp` | Realised HICP inflation in the target month |
| | `dfr`, `regime` | Deposit facility rate and the regime it dates |
| | `lt_mean`, `lt_target_year` | Mean SPF five-year-ahead forecast and its target year |
| `estimation_panel` | `round`, `forecaster`, `forecast` | One row per point forecast, 4'173 rows |
| | further columns | The round-level series joined to each forecast |

The raw sources are listed in the README.

## 7 Errors you might see

The script checks its parameters before doing any work and says what to
change. Five common cases:

-   **`there is no package called 'dplyr'`**: the packages are not
    installed yet. Run `renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)`.
-   **`Database not found: data/thesis.duckdb`**: run
    `build_database.R`.
-   **`anchor must be "ILS" or "LTSPF"`** (or a similar message for
    another parameter): a parameter has a value that is not allowed.
    The message names the parameter and the allowed values.
-   **Standard errors are `NA`**, with a warning that the estimate lies
    at the bound: $\gamma$ and $\rho$ are not identified in that fit.
    The warning names the model and the settings of the fit, for
    example `Model B, delta 0.4000, tau 0.3994, w 0.0000`, which is the
    row `w = 0.0000` of Table 6.3. The estimates and all tables still
    follow.
-   **A DuckDB lock error**: another R session has the database open.
    Close that session.
